key_insight: Travelling wall waves drive net particle rotation, but near-wall transport can reverse direction depending on viscous effects and whether wall material moves only radially or also tangentially.
engineering_relevance: Wave-driven cavity designs could control particle transport by tuning wave imbalance, frequency, and wall kinematics.
method: Decompose Lagrangian drift into Eulerian mean flow and Stokes drift.
Derive closed-form viscous-limit profiles and finite-Womersley profiles by quadrature.
Compare radial and locally arc-length-preserving wall motions using moving-domain simulations.
evidence_signal: At azimuthal order m=2 and Wo²=10, moving-domain simulations recover leading-order drift coefficients for both wall motions.
watch_item: Predictions are leading-order in wall amplitude; larger deformations require validation beyond the reported regime.
paper_title: Lagrangian transport driven by travelling waves in a radially deforming circular cavity
